query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast, equimolar WTaTiVZr refractory high-entropy alloy made from >99.99% pure elemental powders; the comparison baseline was a commercially sourced, powder-sintered pure tungsten plate with coarse equiaxed grains (~100 ± 20 µm).
generation.intervention: The WTaTiVZr alloy was synthesized by arc melting and remelted at least five times, then its phase constitution, microstructure, compressive behavior, temperature-dependent indentation response, and scratch-based fracture toughness were measured and compared with commercially used pure tungsten.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature uniaxial compression used 4 mm × 4 mm cylindrical specimens at an engineering strain rate of 0.001 s^-1. Indentation plastometry used 5 mm cubes, a 1 mm-radius Si3N4 indenter, loads up to 5 kN, and temperatures from room temperature to 500 °C in 100 °C increments. Scratch testing used a 200 µm-radius Rockwell C diamond stylus under a constant 100 N normal load at 0.01 mm/s over 3 mm; tests were repeated at least three times.
generation.structural_mediator: A solidification-segregated dendritic microstructure containing two BCC phases with slightly different lattice parameters: W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions, with V distributed between both phases.
generation.mechanism: The high strength was attributed to multicomponent solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and frictional resistance associated particularly with W and Ta. Improved plasticity and damage tolerance were attributed to Ti, V, and Zr, potentially through reduced valence-electron concentration, dislocation-core modification, improved grain-boundary cohesion, localized plastic deformation, and impeded crack propagation; these mechanistic assignments were presented as interpretations rather than directly isolated causal measurements.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to commercially used pure tungsten, the as-cast WTaTiVZr alloy was expected to provide higher room- and high-temperature strength, greater plastic strain, a lower brittle-to-ductile transition temperature, less scratch-induced cracking and damage, and higher fracture toughness.
generation.baseline: Commercially used powder-sintered pure tungsten: single-phase BCC, coarse equiaxed grains, indentation-derived yield strength of ~700 MPa at room temperature and ~250 MPa at 500 °C, negligible plasticity through 300 °C with ductile behavior emerging near 400 °C, and scratch-based fracture toughness of ~25 ± 1 MPa√m.
generation.boundary: The reported mechanical advantage applies to the as-cast equimolar alloy under quasi-static compression, indentation plastometry from room temperature through 500 °C, and room-temperature scratch testing. The HEA remained relatively brittle at low temperature, showing ~6% room-temperature plastic strain, quasi-cleavage fracture, and radial indentation cracks from 25 to 200 °C; indentation cracking was absent above 200 °C. Irradiation performance and service behavior in an operating fusion environment were not tested.

falsification_experiment.design: XRD, SEM/BSE, EDS, and reported EBSD characterized phases and segregation; uniaxial compression measured yield strength, ultimate compressive strength, and plastic strain; temperature-dependent indentation plastometry measured strength, plastic strain, and crack disappearance; confocal scratch-track profilometry and transverse-force measurements were used to calculate KC from groove perimeter and projected contact area, with SEM assessing cracking and chipping.
measurements: XRD, SEM/BSE, EDS, and reported EBSD characterized phases and segregation; uniaxial compression measured yield strength, ultimate compressive strength, and plastic strain; temperature-dependent indentation plastometry measured strength, plastic strain, and crack disappearance; confocal scratch-track profilometry and transverse-force measurements were used to calculate KC from groove perimeter and projected contact area, with SEM assessing cracking and chipping.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
